Styles apply to `docdesigner::pdf`. They do not apply to `docdesigner::html`, and Snapshot uses its official house style.

You can inspect styles from R:

```r
docdesigner::designer_styles()
docdesigner::designer_style("policy")
docdesigner::designer_gallery()
```

## Built-In Styles

```{r styles-table, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# Generated from the INSTALLED styles rather than written by hand. The static
# table this replaces had drifted badly: by 2026-08-26 all ten of its accent
# colours were wrong, economist was listed as one column when it sets two, and
# sociology and ajs were missing entirely -- the table still described the v1
# styles that the rebuilt ones replaced. Reading the tokens at build time means
# it cannot disagree with what ships.
first_phrase <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", x))
  cuts <- c(regexpr(". ", x, fixed = TRUE), regexpr(": ", x, fixed = TRUE))
  cuts <- cuts[cuts > 0]
  if (length(cuts)) x <- substr(x, 1, min(cuts) - 1)
  x
}
styles <- docdesigner::designer_styles()
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(styles)), function(i) {
  s <- docdesigner::designer_style(styles$style[i])
  data.frame(
    Style    = paste0("`", styles$style[i], "`"),
    Set      = paste0("`", styles$set[i], "`"),
    Use      = first_phrase(styles$description[i]),
    Body     = s$typography$body,
    Accent   = paste0("`", toupper(sub("^#", "", s$color$accent)), "`"),
    Sections = if (isTRUE(s$headings$number_sections)) "numbered" else "unnumbered",
    Columns  = s$page$columns,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
tab <- tab[order(tab$Set, tab$Style), ]
cat(sprintf("The %d built-in styles ship in two sets, `academic` and `public`.

",
            nrow(tab)))
cat(paste(knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE), collapse = "
"), "
")
```

Use a style:

```yaml
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: methods
```

## Create a Style

A style is a folder with a `format.yml` file of design tokens, written as flat
dotted keys — one `key: value` per line:

```yaml
id: my-style
label: My Style
description: A concise description of where this style should be used

typography.body: "Source Serif 4"
typography.heading: "Source Serif 4"
typography.base_size: "10pt"

color.accent: "005EA8"
color.rule: "005EA8"

headings.number_sections: true
headings.h1.scale: 1.30

title.layout: plain
code.highlight: tango
```

The easiest way to start is to scaffold from an existing style and edit only
what differs:

```r
docdesigner::designer_new_style("my-style", from = "minimal")
```

`designer_tokens()` lists every available token, and `STYLE-SPEC.md` documents
them in full. Validate a style against the schema before rendering:

```r
docdesigner::designer_validate_style("my-style")
```

Use a local style by its folder path:

```yaml
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: "path/to/my-style"
```

Keep styles declarative. They describe a visual system through tokens, not
arbitrary R code.
